commands.review_summary:
The PR adds no-op stdout/stderr error listeners to Codex sandbox process and streaming HTTP subprocess spawns and adds a process-RPC pipe-survival regression test.

PR surface: Source +9, Tests +88. Total +97 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection gives a high-confidence path: current main spawns both sandbox subprocess types with stdout/stderr data handlers but no output-stream error handlers; I did not run a live repro in this read-only review.

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap in the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn path.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — real sandbox exec-server run**:

Both paths exercised through a live sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge
(`ensureCodexSandboxExecServerEnvironment` + real shell backend). A child process
writing 200 lines to stdout/stderr is terminated mid-output; the bridge survives and
a second process confirms full functionality. The streaming HTTP subprocess also
survives WebSocket closure mid-stream.

```text
$ node --import tsx sandbox-exec-server-proof.mjs

[23:19:07] === OpenClaw Sandbox Exec-Server Pipe Survival Proof ===
[23:19:07] Starting sandbox exec-server with real shell backend...
[agent/embedded] codex sandbox exec-server started
[23:19:07] Sandbox exec-server started
[23:19:07] WebSocket URL: ws://127.0.0.1:54218/openclaw-7a143c2f-...

[23:19:07] --- Test 1: Process RPC bridge pipe survival ---
[23:19:07] WebSocket connected, listening for JSON-RPC notifications
[23:19:07] Spawning sandbox process "pipe-proof-1" (200-line output loop)
[23:19:07] Process started: {"processId":"pipe-proof-1"}
[23:19:07] Killing process "pipe-proof-1" mid-output via process/terminate RPC
[23:19:07] Terminate result: {"running":true}
[23:19:08] Process closed: exitCode=1, outputChunks=13
[23:19:08] ✓ Bridge survived — WebSocket state is OPEN
[23:19:08] Starting second process "pipe-proof-2" ...
[23:19:08] Second process output: "sandbox-bridge-survived"

[23:19:08] --- Test 2: HTTP streaming bridge pipe survival ---
[23:19:08] Sending streaming HTTP request to local echo server
[23:19:09] Closing WebSocket mid-stream to trigger pipe errors
[23:19:09] Connecting new WebSocket to verify bridge is still alive
[23:19:09] New connection established — bridge survived HTTP stream interruption
[23:19:09] HTTP bridge verification output: "sandbox-bridge-survived"

[23:19:09] === PROOF COMPLETE ===
[23:19:09] Both process RPC and HTTP streaming bridges survived pipe errors.
```

The same no-op error listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`,
confirming this is the repo-standard approach.
